response.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_unit_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, avg_unit_price - AVG(avg_unit_price) OVER () AS deviation FROM inv) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, deviation, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS deviation_minus_country_avg FROM dev ORDER BY (deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country)) IS NULL, deviation_minus_country_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The country is the customer's Customer.Country (as the request says), not Invoice.BillingCountry.
An invoice's average line UnitPrice is the plain average of its InvoiceLine.UnitPrice values (not weighted by Quantity). Invoices with no lines are excluded.
The 'average across all invoices' is the mean of the per-invoice averages, so each invoice counts equally regardless of its number of lines.
The country's average deviation is the mean of the invoice deviations within that country. Ties are broken arbitrarily.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the average UnitPrice across all invoice lines (each line weighted equally), rather than the mean of per-invoice averages.
alternatives.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_unit_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, avg_unit_price - (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM InvoiceLine WHERE InvoiceId IN (SELECT InvoiceId FROM inv)) AS deviation FROM inv) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, deviation, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS deviation_minus_country_avg FROM dev ORDER BY (deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country)) IS NULL, deviation_minus_country_avg DESC LIMIT 10
